title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Estriol (ausschl. Dafo. VCR) ATC G03CD01 f. d. Z. 01.04.26 - 31.03.28 (zzgl. Verlängerungsoption 1x12 Monate)
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Estriol (ausschließlich Darreichungsform VCR), ATC G03CD01, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.04.2026 in Kraft und endet am 31.03.2028 (zzgl. Verlängerungsoption 1x12 Monate). Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

title: T709-809GD ADVANCED COMPUTER VISION METHODS FOR OBJECT DETECTION, CLASSIFICATION ANDSEGMENTATION ON OPTICAL SENSORS IMAGES (EXPRO+)
description: Numerous observations of the sky take place on a daily basis from distributed ground-based andspace-based optical sensors. Typically, faint streak-like features are generated in the images dueto the small size of the objects and relative observation geometry. The detection and segmentationof low signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio streaks poses a major challenge to state-of-the-art tools.Depending on the configured sensitivity in processing tools, it can generate a large number of falsepositive detections. The false detections are caused by artifacts generated by different factors likeoversaturation caused by bright stars, bad pixels or cosmic rays. Similarly, detection, classification,segmentation and tracking of objects like sunspot groups on solar images is a key component foranalysis/forecasting and reaction strategies. For example, reliable knowledge on current activeregions is a crucial factor that can influence Space Weather prediction. However a large challengeof the existing data sources is the large imbalance in class distribution.This activity aims at identifying AI methods to segment such images into background (includingstars etc.) and features, deal with class imbalances, but also to report on the detection probabilityin order to quantify the detection limit for the use of the data to validate existing models. Variousprocessing approaches shall be considered including offline, but also near real-time, as well asconstrained environments for the deployment of AI models like on-board a spacecraft. Anotheraspect that is aimed to be investigated is the digital fusing of data and observations from distributedsensors (e.g. ground and space based telescopes or constellations) and its' correlation. Finally,explainable AI solutions shall be offered for all the algorithms, in order to increase thetrustworthiness of the output predictions for the end-users. T he output of this activity shall contributeto all missions addressing theimprovements of both ground and space based analysis of faintimages.

title: KICK-START THEMATIC CALL: WATER AS FOOD RESOURCE
description: The objective of this Kick Start is to analyse the technical and economic feasibility of new services and solutions for production of food from oceans and inland water bodies. Water as Food Resource studies aim to address the need to increase global food volumes taking into account sustainability and safety concerns. The call addresses four key focus areas. The fishing in remote locations focus area investigates solutions for remote fish farms or shrimp vessels. Precision fishing includes solutions to monitor the environment and manage the infrastructure of fish and shellfish farms. The third area is focused on the production of algae for consumption with positive externalities, such as carbon capture. The last area aims to mitigate illegal practices and increase transparency of current and new fishing activities. The services/solutions put forward should use space assets, such as one or more of Earth observation, Satellite Communication, Satellite Navigation, and Satellite AIS.

title: WEATHER-PROOF OPTICAL COMMUNICATION GROUND TERMINAL (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.050 ) EXPRO+ (RE-ISSUE)
description: The objective of this activity is to evaluate the pros and cons of a weather-proof optical ground terminal (without protective domeenclosure) and to breadboard critical sub-systems. Targeted Improvements:At least 50% faster optical ground station deployment.Description:Today telescopes for ground based free-space optical satellite communication are originating from astronomical telescopes. The current need for optical ground telescopes has changed significantly and other requirements have become design drivers,namely low central obscuration, transmission in the optical C-band, laser transmitter mounting and system integration. Available telescopes need to be mounted in a dome for weather protection and dedicated weatherproof products are not available. This study shall address the requirements of an optical ground terminal that can operate unprotected in the open.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activityrestricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: USER MANAGEMENT SERVICE (UM-SER)
description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected. User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement
